chunks: Among what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, Ibn Muslim, and al-Fudayl, they said: We asked them both about performing the supererogatory prayer in Ramadan at night in congregation.

So they both said: The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, when he had performed the later evening prayer, would depart to his home. Then he would come out at the end of the night to the mosque, stand, and pray. On the first night of the month of Ramadan he came out to pray as he used to pray, and the people formed rows behind him. So he fled from them to his house and left them. They did this for three nights. Then on the fourth day he stood upon his pulpit, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: O people, indeed praying at night in the month of Ramadan, in the supererogatory prayer, in congregation, is a bid'ah, and Salat al-Duha is a bid'ah. Lo, do not gather at night in the month of Ramadan for Salat al-Layl, and do not perform Salat al-Duha, for that is disobedience. Lo, every bid'ah is misguidance, and every misguidance, its path is to the Fire.

Then he descended while saying: A little in a sunnah (prophetic tradition) is better than much in a bid'ah. Do you not see that when he صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم objected, he objected to gathering in it and forbade it, but he did not object to the prayer itself? Had the prayer itself been an objectionable bid'ah, he would have objected to it just as he objected to gathering in it. We have already fully covered what pertains to this chapter in our larger book, so whoever wishes to examine it may do so there.

key_terms.النَّارِ: the Fire, meaning punishment in the hereafter
key_terms.النَّافِلَةِ: supererogatory prayer beyond the obligatory prayers
key_terms.بِدْعَةٌ: a religious innovation introduced into practice
key_terms.سُنَّةٍ: an established prophetic tradition or normative practice
key_terms.صَلَاةَ الضُّحَى: the forenoon prayer mentioned here as an innovation
key_terms.ضَلَالَةٌ: misguidance leading away from the right path

ai.seo_question: Did the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم forbid performing the Ramadan night supererogatory prayer in congregation?
ai.summary: This report states that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم forbade congregational performance of supererogatory night prayers in Ramadan and described it as a bid'ah. It distinguishes between the prayer itself, which is not rejected, and performing it in congregation, which is the prohibited innovation discussed here.
